translations.text: The book of the account of Tobias, son of Tobit, son of Gabael, a descendant of Asahel, of the tribe of Naphtali.
He was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser, king of Persia, from Thisbe, which is south of Kedesh in Naphtali, in Galilee above Asher.
I, Tobit, walked in the way of righteousness and lived uprightly throughout my life. I gave many gifts to help my brothers and my people who went with me to Nineveh in the land of Persia.

While I was still young and living with the Israelites in my own country, all the people of Naphtali and my father abandoned Jerusalem, which had been chosen from all Israel so that all Israel might offer sacrifices there. The sanctuary of the Most High had been consecrated and built there for them, for all generations forever.
All the people who had turned away offered sacrifices to Baal and to the calf, and the house of Naphtali and my father's household joined them.

But I alone would often go to Jerusalem for the festivals, as prescribed for all Israel in the everlasting commandment. I would take the firstfruits of everything I harvested to the priests, the descendants of Aaron, at the altar.
I gave the first tithe of everything to the descendants of Aaron who served in Jerusalem. I also set aside a second tithe and distributed gifts to the needy, and I went to Jerusalem every year.
I gave the third tithe to the poor, as Deborah, my father's mother, had commanded, because my father and mother had left me an orphan.
When I became a man, I married a woman from among my relatives, and by her I had a son, Tobias.
When they were taken captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and relatives ate the food of the Gentiles.
But I kept myself from eating it.
For I remembered God with all my heart.
God granted me favor and goodwill before Shalmaneser, and he appointed me his steward.
I went to Midian and entrusted ten talents of silver to Gabael in Rages, in the land of Midian.
When Shalmaneser died, Sennacherib, whose deeds were evil, reigned in his place. He dismissed me, and I could no longer travel to Midian.
In the days of Shalmaneser, I gave many gifts to help my brothers.
I gave my food to the hungry and my clothing to the naked. If I saw anyone of my people dead and abandoned in the open places of Nineveh, I buried him.
I also secretly buried those whom King Sennacherib killed when he returned in flight from Judea, for he killed many in his anger. The king searched for their bodies but could not find them.
One of the people of Nineveh went to the king and informed against me, saying that I had buried them. I hid when I learned that they wanted to kill me, and I fled in fear.
When they could not find me, they plundered all my possessions and left me nothing except Anna my wife and Tobias my son.

I did not come out for fifty-five days, until two of his sons killed him and fled to Ararat. His son Esarhaddon reigned in his place and appointed Ahikar, son of Asahel, the son of my brother, over his father's entire household and all its administration.
Ahikar petitioned him on my behalf and brought me back into Nineveh. Ahikar was responsible for the seal and the administration of his household, and Akrondesha [?] appointed him second in command.
When I entered my house, they brought my wife Anna back to me. On the day of the festival of Pentecost, the holy feast of seven weeks, they prepared a fine meal for me, and I reclined to eat.
When I saw [?], I said to my son, "Go and bring anyone you find among our brothers who is poor, for I have remembered God. I will wait for you until you return."
When he returned, he said to me, "Father, I found one of our people whose body has been thrown into the marketplace."
I got up without tasting any food and brought him into a house until sunset.
I went into my house, washed, and ate my food in sorrow.
I remembered what Amos said: “Your festivals will turn into mourning.”
Then I wept, and when the sun set, I went and dug a grave and buried him.
The people of the country laughed at me and said, “Is this man not afraid that they will kill him for doing this? For he buries those whom the king has killed.”
That night I lay down to sleep in the [?] of the courtyard, with my face uncovered.

I did not know that there were birds in the [?]. While my face was uncovered, those birds dropped hot droppings into my eyes. I went to physicians, but none helped me. Ahikar supported me until the time when I went alone to Elam.
Anna was occupied with women's work.
She sent it to her employers, and they also gave her a young goat, which she brought to me.
When she came to me, it began to bleat. I said to her, “Where did this young goat come from? If you stole it, return it to its owner, for it is not right to eat something stolen.”

She said to me, “They gave it to me as my wages.” But I did not believe her, and I said to her, “Return it to its owner.” I argued bitterly with her. She answered me, “Where are your charitable deeds and your righteousness? Look, everything about you has become known!”
I was distressed by my suffering, and I prayed and wept.
I said, “You are righteous, Lord, and all your ways are merciful and just. You judge the world with uprightness and righteousness.
Remember me and look upon me, and do not punish me for my sins,

or for the sins of my ancestors, who sinned against you and did not obey your commandment. You handed me over to plunder, mockery, and death, and there was continual disgrace throughout the world and among the nations among whom we have been scattered.
Even now your righteous judgment is just. Deal with me so that my sins and those of my ancestors may be forgiven, for we have not kept your commandment or walked in righteousness before you.

Now deal with me as is pleasing in your sight, and command that my spirit be taken away, so that I may perish and become earth, for it is better for me [?]. False reproach and great sorrow are upon me. Command that I be released from my suffering into the eternal place, and do not turn your face away from me.”
On that day this also happened to Sarah, Raguel's daughter, from Metani in Media: her father's servant women insulted her.

For she had been given in marriage to seven men, and the evil demon Asmodeus had killed them before they could approach her as husband and wife. The women said to her, “Do you not know that your servant women are being strangled? Look, seven men have married you, and not one of them has remained with you.
Why, then, are we being punished on their account? Since they have died, go with them, and may we never see a son or daughter of yours!”
When she heard this, she was deeply distressed and said, “I am my father's only child. If I did this, I would become a disgrace to him and bring his old age down to the grave in anguish.”
She prayed in her house and said, “Blessed are you, Lord my God. May your holy name be blessed. Your name is blessed throughout the world, and all your work is glorious forever.
Now, Lord, I have turned my eyes and my face toward you.
I ask you: remove me from the earth, so that I may no longer hear reproach.
You yourself, Lord, know that I am pure from every sin involving a man.

I have not disgraced my name or my father's name in the land where I was taken captive. I am my father's only child. I have no brother and no close relative, and I am keeping myself for a husband. Yet seven husbands have died on me. Why, then, should I live? But if you are not willing to put me to death, look upon me and have mercy on me, and command that I no longer hear reproach.”
The prayers of both of them were heard before the glory of God's majesty.

He sent Raphael to heal them both: to clear the cloudiness from Tobit's eye, and to give Sarah, Raguel's daughter, to Tobias son of Tobit as his wife, and to destroy the evil demon Asmodeus, because Tobias would inherit her. In those days Tobit returned and entered his house, and Sarah, Raguel's daughter, came down from the upper room.
On that day Tobit remembered the silver he had entrusted to Gabael at Rages in Media.
He thought to himself and said, “Look, I have asked to die. Why should I not call my son Tobias and tell him before I die?”
He called him and said to him, “My son, when I die, bury me properly. Take care of your mother and honor her throughout her life. Do everything she wishes, and do not grieve her.
Remember, my son, that she suffered much pain because of you while you were in her womb. When she dies, bury her with me in the same grave.
Every day, my son, remember the Lord our God. Do not desire to sin or disregard his commandment. Do what is right throughout your life, and do not walk in the path of wrongdoing.
If you do what is right, you will prosper in all your ways and in everything you do. The same is true of everyone who does what is right.
Give alms from your possessions, and do not give grudgingly. Do not turn your face away from a poor person, and God will not turn his face away from you.
Give alms as generously as you can, according to what you have. Even if you have little, do not hesitate to give alms.
For you are storing up a good treasure for yourself.
For almsgiving saves from death on the day of distress and keeps you from going into darkness.
For almsgiving is a good gift before the Most High for those who practice it.

Guard yourself, my son, against all sexual immorality. First, take a wife from the descendants of your ancestors. Do not marry a foreign woman who is not one of your relatives, for we are descendants of the prophets. Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were our ancestors of old. Remember, my son, that they all took wives from among their relatives, and their children were blessed, and their descendants inherited the earth.

Now, my son, love your fellow, and do not be arrogant toward your fellow or toward the children of your people. Take a wife from among their daughters. For where there is pride, there is disgrace and great turmoil; and where there is turmoil, there is hardship and poverty, for it is their mother.

Do not keep overnight the wages of anyone who has worked for you. Instead, pay him promptly from what you have. If you serve God, he will increase your reward. Guard yourself, and be wise in all your work and in all your conduct.
Do not do to anyone what you hate for yourself. Do not drink wine to the point of drunkenness, and do not let drunkenness accompany you on your way.
Give some of your food to the hungry and some of your clothing to the naked. Give alms from everything you have left over.
Scatter your food over the graves of the righteous, but do not give it to sinners.
Seek advice from every wise person, and do not despise advice that will benefit you.

Bless the Lord at all times, and pray to him that your path may be made straight and that he may prosper you in all your work and in all your ways. For all the nations give advice that does not come from God; rather, God himself gives every good thing, and he brings low whomever he wishes, as he wishes. Now, my son, remember my commandment, and do not let it be erased from your heart.
Now I will tell you about the ten talents of silver that I deposited with Gabael son of Gabrias, in Rages in Media.
Do not be afraid, my son, because of your poverty, for the poor will receive a blessing through you if you fear God, and he forgives all your sins, and you do what pleases God in his presence.
Tobias answered and said, “Father, I will do everything you have commanded me.
But how can I collect that silver when I do not know him?”
He gave him a document and said to him, “Find a man to travel with you, and I will pay him his wages while I am alive. Go and collect this silver.”
He went to look for a man and found the angel Raphael, but he did not know that he was an angel.
He said to him, “Can you travel with me to Rages in Media, if you know the region?”
The angel said to him, “I will travel with you. I know the roads there, and I have stayed with Gabael.”
Tobias said to him, “Wait for me while I tell my father Tobit.”

He said to him, “Go, and do not delay.” He went and said to his father, “Look, I have found someone who will travel with me.” His father said to him, “Call him here to me, so that I may know what people he belongs to and whether he is trustworthy enough to travel with you.”
He called him, and he came in, and they greeted one another.
Tobit said to him, “My brother, what people do you belong to, and what country are you from?”

The angel said to him, “Are you asking about my people and my country, or about the wages of the one who will travel with your son?” Tobit said to him, “My brother, I want to know your family and your name.”
He said to him, “I am Azariah, a relative of Ananias the elder, your brother.”

He said to him, “Are you well, my brother? Do not be angry with me because I wanted to know your people and your country. Indeed, you come from a good and blessed family. I know Azariah, of the children of Shemaiah the elder. We went together with them to Jerusalem to worship, and we brought our firstfruits and the tithes of our grain. We did not commit the sin of our ancestors. You come from a great lineage, my brother.”
“But tell me, what shall we give you as your wages? A drachma for each day, along with your food, as you travel with my son?”
I will add more to your wages if you return safely.

They settled the matter in this way. Tobit said to Tobias his son, “Get ready to go.” They made their preparations, and his son prepared their provisions for the journey. His father said to him, “Go with this man. May God, who dwells in heaven, make your journey successful, and may his angel go with you.” The two of them went out and set off, and their son's dog followed them.
His mother Anna wept and said to Tobit, “Why have you sent my son away? Is he not the staff in our hands, the one who goes before us?”
“Let the silver perish!”
“Let what God has given us, by which we live, be a ransom for my son.”
He said to her, “Do not worry, my sister. He will return safely, and you will see him with your own eyes.”
“For the angel of God will go before him and make his journey successful, and he will return safely.” Then Anna stopped weeping.
As they traveled on their way, they reached Tanis, at the river, in the evening, and spent the night there.
The young man went down to wash himself, and a fish darted at him from the river and tried to swallow him.
The angel said to him, “Catch that fish!” The young man caught the fish and brought it out onto the land.
The angel said to him, “Cut open that fish, take its heart, liver, and gall, and keep them carefully.”
The young man did as the angel commanded him. They roasted the fish and ate it. The two of them traveled on and reached Tanis.
The young man said to the angel, “My brother Azariah, what are this fish’s liver, heart, and gall for?”
He said to him, “As for its heart and liver, if an evil demon is tormenting anyone, burn them to make smoke in front of that man or woman, and it will no longer torment them.”
“As for its gall, apply it to the eyes of someone whose eyes are clouded, and he will be healed.”
When they came near Rages, the angel said to him, “My brother, today we will stay with Raguel.”
He is your relative and has one daughter named Sarah. I will speak about her so that they will give her to you as your wife.
“For her inheritance belongs to you, since you are one of her relatives. The daughter is also beautiful and wise.”

“Now listen to me. I will speak to her father, and when we return from Rages, we will hold the wedding feast. Raguel cannot give her to another man because of the law of Moses; and if he gives another preference, [?] will die. For you have the right to her inheritance before anyone else.”
The young man said to the angel, “My brother Azariah, I have heard that this girl was married to seven men, and they all died at the wedding.”
“Now I am my father’s only child. I am afraid that when I go in, I may die and bring my father’s and mother’s lives down in sorrow. They have no other son to bury them.”

The angel said to him, “Do you not remember what your father commanded you—that you should take a wife from among your relatives? Now listen to me, my brother, and do not let the demon trouble you, for this very night she will be given to you as a wife from among your relatives.”
“When you enter your room, take some glowing incense embers, put some of that fish’s liver and heart on them, and make smoke with them.”

When that demon smells it, he will flee and never return. When you go in to her, both of you cry out to the merciful God, and he will save you and have mercy on you. So do not be afraid, for he has prepared you from eternity. You will save her, and she will go with you. I tell you that you will have children by her. When Tobias heard this, he was amazed, and he became deeply attached to her. They reached Ecbatana.
They entered Raguel’s house, and Sarah received them and made them welcome. They greeted her in the same way, and she brought them into the house.
Raguel said to his wife Edna, “How remarkably this young man resembles Tobit, my relative!”
Raguel said to them, “Where are you from, my brothers?” They said to him, “We are descendants of Naphtali who were taken captive to Nineveh.”
Raguel said to them, “Do you know my brother Tobit?”
They said to him, “Yes, we know him. Is he alive and well?” Tobias said to him, “He is my father.”
Raguel sprang up, kissed him, and wept.
He blessed him and said to him, “You are the son of a blessed man.” He told him that Tobit had lost his sight. When Raguel heard that his sight had been destroyed, he was distressed and wept.

His wife Edna and his daughter Sarah did likewise. They welcomed them joyfully, slaughtered sheep, and served them. Afterward, when evening came, Tobias said to Azariah, “My brother Azariah, speak about what you told me on the road, and let the matter be settled.”
When Raguel heard Tobias saying this to the angel, he said to Tobias, “Eat and drink together, and be happy.”
For this daughter of mine is yours, and you will marry her. I will tell you the truth about this daughter of mine.

I gave this daughter of mine in marriage to seven men, and as soon as they went in to her, they died during the night. But eat and enjoy yourself for now.” Tobias said, “I will taste nothing at all until you settle and confirm this matter for me.”
Raguel said to him, “Take her from now on, according to the law.”
“For you are her kinsman, and she is your wife. May the merciful God guide you in what is good.”
He called his daughter Sarah.
He took her hand and gave her to Tobias to be his wife. He said to him, “Here, take her according to the law of Moses, and bring her to your father.” Then he blessed them.
He called his wife Edna, took a document, and sealed it. They began to eat. He called Edna and said to her, “My sister, prepare another room and bring her into it.”
She did as he told her and brought her there. She wept and caught her daughter’s tears.
She said to her, “Take courage, my daughter. May the Lord of heaven and earth give you joy and gladness in place of your sorrow.”
When they had finished supper, they brought Tobias in to her.
When he entered, he remembered his words. He took burning coals for incense, put some of the heart and liver of that fish on them, and made smoke.
When that demon smelled its odor, [?] as far as the upper region of Egypt, and that angel bound the demon.
When the two of them were left alone, Tobias rose from his bed and said to her, “Get up, my sister. Let us pray to God, so that he may have mercy on us.”

Tobias began by saying, “Blessed are you, Lord, God of our ancestors. May your holy name be blessed and praised forever and ever. May the heavens and everything you have created bless you. You made Adam.”
“You gave him Eve to be his wife and to comfort him, and from them the human race was born. You said, ‘It is not good for a man to be alone; let us make him a companion to help him.’”
“And now, Lord, I take this woman, my kinswoman, not out of lust but in righteousness. Send your mercy upon me and upon her, so that we may rejoice.”
She said with him, “Amen.”
The two of them spent that night together. Then Raguel got up, went out, and dug a grave.
Saying, “Perhaps he too will die.”
Raguel returned to his house and said to his wife Edna:
“Send a servant girl to see whether he is alive. If not, let us bury him without anyone knowing.”
The servant girl went, opened the door, and found them both sleeping.
She returned and told them that they were alive.

Raguel blessed God and said, “Blessed are you, Lord, with every pure and holy blessing. May your holy ones bless you for all your works, and may all your angels and your chosen ones bless you forever.”
Blessed are you, Lord, because you have made me glad. What happened to me was not what I had expected; rather, you dealt with me according to your great mercy.
Blessed are you, Lord, because you have had mercy on these two only children. You have shown them your goodness, Lord, so that through your mercy they may complete their lives in safety and joy.
Then he ordered his servants to fill in that grave.
He held a feast for them for fourteen days.
Then Raguel made Tobias swear that he would not leave or go away until the fourteen days of the wedding celebration were over.
After that he could go, taking half of Raguel’s possessions, and return safely to his father. After Raguel’s death, Tobias and his wife would receive what remained.
Tobias called Raphael and said to him, “My brother Azariah, take two young men and camels with you.
Go to Gabael at Rages in Media, collect the ten talents of silver, and invite him too to the feast.
For Raguel has made me swear not to leave until the feast is over.
But my father is counting the days, and if I delay, he will be deeply distressed.”
Raphael went and reached Gabael, and gave him the document. Gabael brought out the sealed bag and gave it to Raphael.
They set out together in the morning and arrived at the feast. Tobias blessed him when he brought him the silver.
Meanwhile Tobit, Tobias’s father, was counting the days. When the time allotted for their journey had passed and they had not returned,
he said, “Perhaps our son has been put to shame, or Gabael has died and he has found no one to give him the silver.”
He was deeply distressed.
His wife said to him, “My son is dead, and that is why he is delayed.” She began to mourn him.
She said, “[?] my son grieves me, though he was not one to trouble me, the light of my eyes.”
He said to her, “Be quiet and do not worry. He is alive.”

But she said to him, “You be quiet too, and do not deceive me. My son is dead.” Every day she went out to the road by which he had gone and wept for him. By day she ate no food, and at night she did not stop weeping for her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the feast were over—the days during which Raguel had made him swear not to leave until the wedding feast was finished.
Then, when the days of the feast were over, Tobias said to Raguel, “Send me away now, for my father and mother have given up on me and no longer hope to see me.”
His father-in-law said to him, “Stay with me, and I will send someone to your father to tell him news of you.”
Tobias said to him, “No, send me back to my father.”
Raguel rose and gave him Sarah his wife and half their possessions, both servants and livestock.

He blessed them and said to them, “May the Lord of heaven show you kindness, my children, before I die.” He said to his daughter, “Honor your parents-in-law, for from now on they are your family. May we hear good news about you.” He kissed her. Edna said to Tobias, “My dear brother, may the Lord of heaven prosper you and give you a son by Sarah my daughter. See to it that I may rejoice before God. Now I have entrusted my daughter to your care; do not cause her sorrow.”
Afterward Tobias departed and blessed God because he had made his journey successful. Raguel and his wife Edna blessed him. They traveled on and came near Nineveh.
Then Raphael said to Tobias, “My brother, do you not know the condition in which you left your father?
Come, let us go ahead of your wife and prepare the house.
Take the fish’s gall with you.” The two of them went, and that boy who had followed them went with them.
Meanwhile Anna was sitting by the road, waiting for her son’s arrival.
She saw him as he was coming [?], and she told his father, saying, “Look, your son has come, and the man who went with him has come too.”
Raphael said to Tobias, “I know that your father’s eyes will be opened.
Apply this gall to his eyes. When it is applied, he will rub them, and that cloudiness will come out of them, and his sight will be restored.”
Anna ran and threw her arms around her son’s neck. His mother said to him, “Now I can die, since I have seen you, my son.” And they both wept.
Tobit went out to the door, and they embraced. His son ran and lifted his father up and applied that gall to his eyes.
He said to him, “Have faith, Father, that you will recover.”
When he applied it, his father rubbed his eyes.
The film came away from his eyes, and he saw his son.
He threw his arms around his son’s neck and wept, saying, “Blessed are you, Lord, and blessed be your name forever, and blessed are all your holy angels.
For you have punished us and shown us mercy, and now I have seen Tobias my son.” Then his son went inside rejoicing and told his father all the great things that had happened to him.
Tobit went out joyfully to welcome his daughter-in-law, blessing God at the gate of Nineveh. Those who saw him walking were amazed and said, “How can he see?”

Tobit praised God before them because the God of heaven had shown him mercy. When Tobit reached Sarah, his daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said to her, “Have you arrived safely, my daughter? Blessed be God, who brought you to us, and may he bless your father and your mother.” There was great joy among all his relatives who lived in Nineveh.
Ahikar and Nasbas, his brother’s son, came.
They celebrated joyfully for seven days.
Then Tobit called Tobias and said to him, “My son, see to the wages of that man who went with you, and it is right that you give him something extra.”
Tobias said to his father, “Father, I would lose nothing if I gave him half of these possessions that I have brought.”
“For he brought me back to you safely, healed my wife, brought the silver, and likewise healed you.”
His father said to him, “You have spoken rightly.”
He called the angel and said to him, “Take half of all the possessions you brought with you, and go in peace.”

At that time Raphael called both of them, took them aside, and said to them, “Bless God and praise him. Magnify his name and acknowledge him before every living creature for all the good things he has done for you. Give thanks to God and glorify his name. Tell of God's deeds and make them known with honor. Do not be slow to praise him.”
“For it is good to conceal a king’s secret, but God’s work should be made known through deeds. Do good, and evil will not overtake you.
Prayer with peace, charity, and righteousness is good. A little gained honestly is better than great wealth gained unjustly, and giving to the poor is better than storing up gold.
For charity saves from death and cleanses from every sin. Those who practice righteousness and give to the poor will enjoy fullness of life.
But those who sin hate their own lives.
Now I will hide nothing from you. I told you that it is good to conceal a king’s secret, but God’s work should be made known with honor.
When you and Sarah your bride prayed, I brought the remembrance of your prayer before the Most Holy One. And when you buried the dead, I was with you then.
When you did not hesitate, but rose and left your meal and went to bury a corpse, and did not forget to do good, I was with you then.
And God sent me to heal you and to comfort Sarah, your bride, in her sorrow.
I am Raphael, an angel, one of the seven holy archangels who carry up the prayers of the holy ones and enter before the glory of the Great and Holy One.
When they heard this, both of them were astonished and fell on their faces because they were afraid.
And he said to them, “Do not be afraid. Bless the Lord your God.
For thanks are not due to me; rather, the will of your God brought me. Therefore bless the God of righteousness forever.
Throughout all the days when I appeared to you and you saw my appearance, I did not eat or drink with you.
And now believe in God, for I am ascending to the one who sent me, and I came to write these books.”
Then he rose and went away, and they saw him no more.
And they believed in all the work of the Lord, great and awesome, and because the angel of the Lord had appeared to them.
And Tobit prayed a prayer of joy and said, “Blessed be God, who lives forever, and whose kingdom lasts forever and ever.
He punishes and shows mercy; he brings down into Sheol and raises up, and no one can escape from his hand.
Praise him, all you children of Israel, before all the nations among whom he has scattered us.
There he has shown his mercy toward us. Exalt him before all humanity, for he is our Lord, and he is God our Father for all eternity.
He punishes us for all our sins, but he will again show us mercy and gather us from all the nations among whom he has scattered us.

If we return to him with all our heart and all our soul, to do what is right before him, then he will return to us and will not hide his face from us. See what he has done for us, and believe in him with all your heart and all your soul. Bless God and exalt the eternal King in the land where you have been taken captive. As for me, in the land where I have been taken captive, I believe in him and proclaim his power and greatness to a sinful people. Turn back, sinners, and do what is right before my Lord. Who knows whether my God will choose to show his mercy toward you?
My soul will exalt the King of heaven. I praise the greatness of the God of righteousness in everything.
Believe in him in righteousness, Jerusalem, holy city. Will he not punish you for your righteous deeds? And again he will [?] the children of the righteous.

Praise the Lord well, and bless the eternal King, so that his dwelling may be rebuilt within you with joy, and those who are captives may rejoice in you there, and those who are hated may love one another because of you, throughout all generations forever.

For many nations will come from far away to the name of the Lord, and they will bring gifts to the eternal King and to the King of heaven. From generation to generation they will praise you, Lord, and give glory to your name.
Cursed are all who hate you, and blessed forever are all who love you.
You will rejoice in the children of the righteous, for they will gather together and bless you, Lord, because blessed are those who love you and rejoice in your name.
And blessed are all who grieve over your suffering, for they will rejoice in you when they see all your glory, and they will rejoice forever.
Our soul will bless God, the great King.
For Jerusalem will be built with sapphire, emerald, and precious stones—her courtyards and her ramparts—and her gates with pure gold.
And her square will be made of crystal and carbuncle stones of Ophir, and of stones of Ophir.
And in all her streets they will say, ‘Hallelujah!’ They will praise him and say, ‘Blessed be God forever and for all eternity.’”
After this, Tobit stopped praying.
He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight, and after fifty-eight years he saw again. He gave alms and continued to grow in his fear of God.
He grew very old and called his son and his son's children. He said to him, “My son, take your children, for I have grown old and am close to death.

Go to Media, for I know that everything the prophet Jonah said about Nineveh will happen: it is going to be overthrown. But in Media there will be peace for a time. Our brothers will be scattered in exile away from all the blessed land. Jerusalem will become desolate, and the house of God within it will be burned with fire and become desolate.

God will again have mercy on them and bring them back to their land. They will rebuild his house, though not as it was before, until the ages of the world are fulfilled. After this they will return from their captivity, and Jerusalem will be rebuilt in glory. Within it the house of God will be rebuilt with splendid masonry for all generations forever.
All the nations will abandon their gods and turn to righteousness.

They will fear God and bless him, and the people will believe in him. God will have mercy on his people, and all who fear God in righteousness and uprightness will rejoice and show mercy to their brothers.
And now, my son, leave [?] Nineveh, because what Jonah the prophet said will indeed come to pass.
But you, keep the law and the commandments. Be merciful and love righteousness, so that things may go well for you.

Bury me properly, and your mother with me. Do not remain in Nineveh, my son. Consider what Haman did to Ahikar, how he brought him from light into darkness, and whether he was repaid according to his wickedness. Ahikar is alive, but Haman received his punishment and himself went down into darkness. Manasseh gave alms and acted righteously, and he escaped the deadly punishment they had prepared for him. But Haman fell into that trap and died.

Now, my son, see how almsgiving saves those who practice it and bears the fruit of righteousness.” After saying this, Tobit died, and his spirit departed as he lay on his bed. He was one hundred and fifty-eight years old, and they buried him with honor.
When Anna, his mother, died, Tobias, Tobit's son, buried her with his father. Then Tobias went with his wife and children to Raguel in Ecbatana.
Raguel and his wife Edna grew old and died. Tobias buried his parents-in-law with honor and inherited all their possessions, as well as those of his father Tobit.
Before he died, Tobias heard of the destruction of Nineveh, just as his father had told him. Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus heard of the destruction of Nineveh and rejoiced.
Tobias died at the age of one hundred and twenty and [?].
